Icosian Mite
CR 3

This mite is tiny, no larger than a coin. Its body, shaped like a twenty-sided die, is a translucent yellow, like crystal or gemstone. Two yellow eyes with black slit pupils stare at you from one of its faces, and eight clawed limbs protrude from its sides. As it skitters towards you, you feel a chill run down your spine.

XP 800
CN Tiny outsider (vermin)
Init +3; Senses darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +4

DEFENSE

AC 18, touch 15, flat-footed 15 (+3 Dex, +2 size, +3 natural)
hp 13 (3d8)
Fort +3, Ref +4, Will +1; Immune mind-affecting effects

OFFENSE

Speed 20 ft., climb 20 ft.
Melee bite +8 (1d3-4 plus bad luck)
Space 2-1/2 ft.; Reach 0 ft.

STATISTICS

Str 3, Dex 17, Con 10, Int —, Wis 10, Cha 2
Base Atk +2; CMB +3, CMD 10 (14 vs. trip)
Feats Weapon Finesse
Skills Climb +11, Stealth +15; Racial Modifiers +4 Perception
SQ Twist Luck

ECOLOGY

Environment any ruins
Organization solitary, pair, or infestation (3–12)
Treasure none

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Bad Luck Bite (Su)

An Icosian mite’s bite is feared not for its damage but for the curse it carries. A creature bitten by an Icosian mite must make a DC 13 Will save or suffer a -2 penalty on all d20 rolls for 24 hours. This is a cumulative effect, each bite potentially causes more bad luck. Only a remove curse or similar spell can remove this effect.

Twist Luck (Su)

Any to-hit roll on a 20-sided die versus this creature that comes up as a natural 20, is instead considered a natural 1. Icosian mites only take critical hits from attacks with a threat range better than 20.

The Icosian mite is a peculiar and dreaded creature, tiny in size but capable of causing great misfortune. It resembles a minuscule spider with an exoskeleton shaped like a twenty-sided die, each facet numbered as if part of the die itself. Its eight legs are thin and agile, allowing it to move with surprising speed and precision. The mite’s bite is said to bring bad luck, a superstition that has been proven true by those unfortunate enough to suffer its effects.

Adventurers are advised to approach with caution, for while the Icosian mite may not pose a significant physical threat, the bad luck it bestows can lead to disastrous consequences.
